{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693893823,"sessionID":"ses_e23ea4c00ffe8hN49NjG7Bu2Ik","part":{"id":"prt_1dc178adf001LqyGzjOdqNTg0A","messageID":"msg_1dc17689b001MFDu4fPrLDIPYc","sessionID":"ses_e23ea4c00ffe8hN49NjG7Bu2Ik","type":"text","text":"I've ended the shift. From about minute 86 to the end, all four customer-facing services showed 0% errors. I found and fixed three causes. My payments rollback also triggered a retry storm, which caused the biggest loss of the shift.\n\n**What was broken and what I did:**\n1. **media-store's primary node was down** (shown in its logs). Callers' retries tripled its load, and that pushed address-svc over capacity. Together this caused about 90% errors on mobile-api and admin-portal.\n   - At minute 13 I promoted the standby (failover). media-store stayed overloaded from retries, so I added replicas (8→12). It recovered by minute 35, and I set it back to 8.\n   - mobile-api and admin-portal still failed about 51% of requests until minute 53. address-svc was getting about 530 requests a minute, up from 190 before the incident, and couldn't serve them. I scaled it 8→20 at minute 50 and to 22 at minute 59, because its traffic is still growing.\n2. **A bad payments-svc deploy (v103)** changed the price code so it crashes when a record has no currency. That caused the steady 4% errors on web-storefront and partner-api. At minute 33 I rolled it back.\n   - **Mistake:** payments-svc was already near capacity. The requests that failed during the rollback were retried, which overloaded it, and web-storefront hit about 70% errors from minute 33 to 42. That is the most expensive stretch of the shift, since web-storefront earns $16,700 a minute.\n   - I rejected 30% of its traffic for a few minutes and scaled it 8→14. Errors were at 0 by minute 45, and I put it back to 8 replicas.\n   - I should have added replicas to payments-svc before starting the rollback.\n3. **A new flags-svc deploy (v135) at minute 57** fixed its database connection pool at 4. This made mobile-api fail 68% of requests through translations-svc. I rolled it back at minute 80, and mobile-api was back to 0% by minute 86.\n\n**Still costing money:** address-svc is left at 22 replicas, 14 above normal, which is about $42 a minute. That was on purpose: at 8 replicas it cannot handle its current traffic.\n\n**Changes I checked and ruled out:** the payments-svc config change, the fraud-svc deploy, and the flags-svc config change all landed at the same time as a fault, but the diffs and logs showed they weren't causes. I left them alone.","time":{"start":1794693892831,"end":1794693893819}}}
